feature1.prompt: The clone function fails when one or more instance parameters are estimator types (i.e., when classes are passed instead of instances). This issue leads to a TypeError because the function attempts to access the get_params method on a type rather than on an instance. The expected behavior is that when an estimator type is provided as a parameter, the clone function should handle it gracefully without raising an error. For example, calling clone(StandardScaler(with_mean=StandardScaler)) should complete successfully without any get_params() errors.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature targets the core functionality in the clone function. You need to update the condition in the elif block in sklearn/base.py so that it also checks if the estimator is a type by using isinstance(estimator, type). The updated logic must continue to preserve the existing behavior when estimator parameters are instances. Pay close attention to ensuring that this modification does not affect tests for other use cases of the clone function.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sklearn/base.py; Function: clone; Modify the code around lines 48-60 where the condition is updated from 'elif not hasattr(estimator, 'get_params'):' to 'elif not hasattr(estimator, 'get_params') or isinstance(estimator, type):'.

feature2.prompt: The clone function currently fails when estimator types are used as parameters, which disrupts workflows that rely on wrapping estimators and storing them by their classes. This feature focuses on verifying that the updated clone function now correctly handles such scenarios, ensuring that no errors occur when an estimator type is passed. The desired behavior is that an estimator provided with a parameter of its class type should be cloned without triggering a TypeError. This is particularly important for projects that wrap sklearn estimators and require storing the classes (not instances) as parameters.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature involves creating a dedicated test case to validate the new behavior of the clone function. You should add a test that calls clone on an estimator with a type as one of its parameters and assert that the parameter remains a type in the cloned object. The test must check that no errors are raised during the cloning process and that the correct behavior is maintained when handling estimator types.
feature2.entrypoint: File: sklearn/tests/test_base.py; Add a new test function named test_clone_estimator_types following the existing test definitions. Use the provided diff patch as guidance for the test structure and assertions.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the clone function in sklearn/base.py and the test suite in sklearn/tests/test_base.py.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Ensure that the modifications in the core clone function (feature1) are fully validated by the newly added test case (feature2). The new test should only pass when feature1 has been correctly implemented, and all other tests must continue to pass.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on feature1 and feature2 need to coordinate closely to confirm that the updated behavior in the clone function covers all intended use cases. It is important to discuss edge cases and verify that the new test captures the correct behavior without disrupting existing functionality.
